newsitem.title: USA: Davel sees Q3 net off, rev up vs year ago.
newsitem.headline: Davel sees Q3 net off, rev up vs year ago.

text.p: Davel Communications Group Inc said Thursday it expected to report third-quarter earnings of $0.22 to $0.24 a share, down from $0.26 in the corresponding period of 1995.
The company, which owns and operates pay telephones, said it expected to post a three percent increase in revenue to $12 million from $11.7 million.
Net income for the 1996 third quarter is expected to exceed $1 million, down from $1,157,444 in the year-ago period.
Analysts have estimated third-quarter net income of $0.24 a share, according to First Call survey.
The company said it expected to report the third-quarter results on November 14.
Chief Executive Robert Hill said in the announcement that he was pleased with the company's performance.
"Davel's cost controls and disciplined acquisition strategy have allowed us to maintain profitability in a very trying period for the pay phone industry," Hill said.

"With the implementation of the long-awaited Telecommunications Act of 1996 upon us, we look forward to operating in a more competitive market and finally receiving compensation for all calls placed from our pay phones," Hill said.
Separately, the company said it completed its purchase of the assets of Pay Telephone America Ltd, comprised of 1,000 installed pay phones and other equipment, for a price of $3.5 million.
